title: Fibre products of algebraic spaces and pullback of etale coverings
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $F,G,H$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $F\to H$, $G\to H$ be morphisms. The sheaf fibre product $F\times_HG$ is an algebraic space and is a fibre product in the category of algebraic spaces over $S$. If $\{H_i\to H\}_{i\in I}$ is a jointly surjective etale family of algebraic spaces and $G\to H$ is any morphism, then $\{G\times_HH_i\to G\}_{i\in I}$ is again a jointly surjective etale family. Here scheme fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product], and etale maps of algebraic spaces are representable as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]; in particular $G\times_HH_i$ is a scheme if $G$ is a scheme and $H_i\to H$ is etale. In the joint-surjectivity clause, $|X|$ denotes the set of equivalence classes of maps $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, with $K$ a field [def-weil-field]; two maps represent the same point if their pullbacks to some common field extension agree. A family is jointly surjective if the union of its images on these sets is all of the target point set.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sheaf-pullback-diagonal] to the underlying sheaves and the representable diagonals from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The explicit compatible-pair cone is limiting pointwise (Mathlib Types.pullbackLimitCone and evaluationJointlyReflectsLimits). The sheaf-to-presheaf functor preserves the chosen sheaf pullback; uniqueness of pullbacks identifies its underlying presheaf with the compatible-pair presheaf. Transport the representable diagonal through this isomorphism and its induced product isomorphism. Transport of a representable-with-property predicate is proved directly by transporting each representing pullback square.

source.place: Tags 04T9 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal), first two conditions of the proof, and 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces), universal property.

proof.text: Choose atlases of F and G using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-trf-fibre-product-atlas-tests] with the representable diagonal of H. It supplies a scheme D representing the presheaf pullback of the two atlases and a representable etale, surjective atlas map to the presheaf pullback of F and G. Compose with the representing isomorphism at the source and with the comparison to the underlying chosen sheaf pullback at the target. Transporting the scheme-test squares preserves etaleness and surjectivity. Together with step 1 these give IsAlgebraicSpace of the chosen sheaf pullback.

source.place: Tag 04T9 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal), last paragraph: construction and scheme tests of the atlas.

proof.text: The universal property of the chosen sheaf pullback gives the unique lift of any compatible pair of sheaf maps. Morphisms of algebraic spaces are the morphisms of their underlying sheaves by [def-trf-algebraic-space], so apply the ordinary categorical pullback lift and its projection equations; pullback.hom_ext proves uniqueness. No additional hypothesis about the test algebraic space is needed.

source.place: Tags 04T9 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal), first two conditions of the proof, and 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces), universal property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-presheaf-pullback-etale-point-lifting] to the underlying sheaves. Transport its IsEtale assertion along the explicit-to-chosen pullback isomorphism from step 1. For joint surjectivity, apply the lemma to a field-valued point of G, then apply the same isomorphism to its lifted compatible pair; the projection equation preserves the required equality. This works for any index type, including the empty one. For the scheme special case, apply the lemma with a singleton family and compose its representing isomorphism with the inverse explicit-to-chosen pullback comparison.

lean.statement: theorem fibreProduct_isAlgebraicSpace {S : Scheme.{u}} (F G H : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : F ⟶ H) (g : G ⟶ H) : IsAlgebraicSpace (Limits.pullback f.hom g.hom) ∧ ∀ (Q : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : Q ⟶ F) (b : Q ⟶ G), a ≫ f = b ≫ g → ∃! l : Q.obj ⟶ Limits.pullback f.hom g.hom, l ≫ Limits.pullback.fst f.hom g.hom = a.hom ∧ l ≫ Limits.pullback.snd f.hom g.hom = b.hom
lean.note: The three declarations jointly render the node: sheaf-pullback closure with the full-subcategory universal property; preservation of representable etaleness and joint surjectivity on point classes; and representability of the fibre product when G is a scheme. The point-image condition is expanded on field-valued representatives after extension, via the new definition node.
